facts.text: The project serves a STARService of about 150 RPCs for Hamilton STAR liquid handler control and a ResourceService for deck resources
RemoteSTARBackend is a ConnectRPC client that acts as a drop-in replacement for STARBackend
RemoteSTARBackend.connect builds a STARServiceClientSync at the given base URL
STARServiceImpl wraps a real STARBackend and create_star_app serves it
The service's Stop RPC awaits STARBackend.stop
The client's halt is an async def that calls the synchronous client's halt with a HaltRequest and no timeout_ms
STARServiceClientSync.halt is a plain def that returns execute_unary for the Halt method
The service's Setup RPC awaits STARBackend.setup
The service's Halt RPC awaits STARBackend.halt
The client reads num_channels from the service and exposes it as a property
The client has a move-all-pipetting-channels-to-Z-safety command
The client reads all channel Y positions as a map
The client reads all channel Z positions as a map
The client reads the iSWAP version string

The client's low-level aspirate_pip takes per-channel lists, among them tip_pattern, x_positions, y_positions, aspiration_volumes and aspiration_speed, each defaulting to a one-element list, and calls the synchronous client
The client's low-level dispense_pip takes per-channel lists, among them tip_pattern, x_positions, y_positions, dispense_volumes and dispense_speed, and calls the synchronous client
The STAR service protocol declares the Halt RPC
The client package is installed from PyPI and connects to a STAR server at a base URL

safe_state.description: none proven: the runtime latches and refuses new calls; the e-stop sends the upstream Halt RPC (forwarded to PyLabRobot's STARBackend.halt, which is not in the clone; it cannot be sent while another RPC blocks the event loop) and reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held
